missing_methods.intent: Assert tell your experience text is truncated
missing_methods.label: Assert tell your experience text is truncated
missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should verify that the text entered in the 'tell your experience' field is truncated to a maximum character limit. It should: 1) Get the current text value from the feedback text field using get_entered_text() or similar method, 2) Compare the length of the entered text against the expected maximum length parameter, 3) Verify that the character count display shows the truncation (e.g., '500/500' if max is 500), 4) Return True if text is properly truncated, False otherwise, 5) Optionally raise an assertion error with details if truncation validation fails. The method should handle edge cases where text might be at or below the limit.

input_parameters.name: expected_max_length
input_parameters.description: The maximum character length allowed for the feedback text field

output_parameters.description: Returns True if text is truncated correctly, False otherwise

missing_methods.architectural_notes: This method belongs in feedback.py because it validates a specific behavior of the feedback text input field. It should leverage existing methods like get_entered_text() and get_feedback_text_char_count() to perform the validation. The truncation logic is a core aspect of the feedback form's data validation requirements.
